title: Can I Survive MORE Drawback Chess?
summary: Drawback Chess vs online humans (2+1); goal 5 wins. Drawbacks seen: Scorched Earth, My Kingdom for a Horse, Farsighted, Lame Duck, True Gentleman, Scouting Ahead, Absolution. Win by capturing the king.
rules: Standard setup and moves; each player is dealt one secret random drawback (card with Easy-Hard difficulty slider); the opponent's drawback is revealed when the game ends ('Your opponent's drawback was ...').
No check/checkmate: kings may move into or stay in attack; capturing the enemy king wins.
Breaking or failing your drawback condition makes you lose (or the move is simply illegal, depending on drawback wording).
Players may chat/rename to bluff or reveal drawbacks.

Drawbacks in this video: Scorched Earth - you can't move to a square that you've moved from (visited squares tinted red/pink). My Kingdom for a Horse - you lose if your opponent captures one of your knights. Farsighted - your pieces can't capture nearby pieces (exact distance not captured). Scouting Ahead - as long as you have a pawn, you cannot move non-pawns ahead of your most advanced pawn. Absolution - when one of your non-bishop pieces captures, it must start a turn adjacent to one of your bishops before it can capture again. Lame Duck; True Gentleman.
win_condition: Capture the enemy king. Goal: 5 wins.
